system.one_liner: Gene expression prediction from DNA: longer input sequences do not help, so the paper integrates proximal multimodal epigenomic signals, which contribute unequally.

content.variant_note: six titled panels in a 2x3 grid, three schematics of the biology and models over three measured charts, each carrying one finding of the motivation
content.argues: Extending the input sequence does not improve expression prediction; nearby multimodal epigenomic signals matter, contribute unequally, and models over-depend on background signals.
content.subject: Chromatin looping, an SSM long-sequence model with three limitations, stacked epigenomic tracks, and three charts of input length and signal ablations.

lessons.what_to_learn: A motivation figure can be a 2x3 board: three claim-titled schematics (the setting, the baseline's limitations, the idea) over three measured charts that back each claim, so the paper's premise is argued before any method is drawn.
lessons.suits: Position or motivation figures that argue against a prevailing practice (longer inputs, bigger models) using one schematic and one measurement per claim.

evidence: (b) Current longsequence models suffer from technical limitations.
(c) Multimodal epigenomic signals provide cell-type specific regulatory information.
removing background signals during testing from models trained on all signals causes severe performance degradation

summary: The paper predicts gene expression from DNA sequence and argues that extending the input length is not what helps; proximal multimodal epigenomic signals matter more and contribute unequally. Figure 1 is a six-panel motivation figure. Three schematics come first: (a) enhancers E1 and E2 reaching a TSS through chromatin looping, (b) an SSM long-sequence model reading a 200 kb input, with a Weak and Strong gradient arrow and three red-cross limitations (recency bias, fixed hidden states, performance degradation), and (c) H3K27ac, DNase and Hi-C tracks around a ~1kb window. Three measured charts follow: a line chart of Pearson correlation against input length for Seq2Exp and Caduceus, a bar chart of signal contributions and a bar chart of test-time ablations. Serif titles, flat colour, white ground.
summary_zh: 论文指出基因表达预测的关键不是加长输入序列，而是近端多模态表观基因组信号。图1为六格动机图：上排三幅示意图（染色质环、SSM的三项缺陷、信号轨道），下排三幅实测图（输入长度折线图、信号贡献与消融柱状图）。
notes: Prior kinds changed: contribution-mosaic (finding-cards) is primary because the six panels are separate findings, not alternatives, so side-by-side-contrast is dropped; concept-schematic stays for (a)-(c). The meaning of the Weak/Strong gradient arrow is read from the later text about recency bias. The grey funnel in (c) is a wide-to-narrow wedge, not a zoom inset. Chart (d) is a JPEG; (e) and (f) are vector, their tick text is not in the live text layer.
